title: Robo-advisor vs. AI investing agent vs. financial advisor: what’s the difference?
summary: A robo-advisor runs a portfolio for you, an AI investing agent helps you decide, and a financial advisor plans your whole financial life with you.
body_markdown:
## What does an AI investing agent do?


An AI investing agent, as we use the term, works with the accounts you already have. It doesn’t hold your money or manage a portfolio, and it comes to you when something matters so you can decide what to do.


Astor is a personal investing agent on iPhone and in iMessage. It connects to brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts at most major US institutions, like Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase, through Plaid. It follows every position you own, plus the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch them, and texts you what happened, why it matters to you and what you could do. You can ask it anything about your actual holdings, set[scheduled alerts](https://www.astor.app/blog/scheduled-alerts) , and, with[Text to Trade](https://www.astor.app/blog/introducing-text-to-trade) on Max plans, turn an idea into a proposed basket of companies that only executes in your own Robinhood agentic account after you approve each trade.


The limits are worth saying plainly. An agent doesn’t build a financial plan, and Astor doesn’t do budgeting, tax filing or estate planning. The AI can be wrong, which is why Astor shows the reasoning and sources behind every alert and you make the call. Not every AI investing tool is a registered adviser, either, so check before you rely on one. We compare a few in[SEC-registered AI investment advisers](https://www.astor.app/blog/sec-registered-ai-investment-advisers) , and[what is a personal investing agent](https://www.astor.app/blog/what-is-a-personal-investing-agent) goes deeper on the category.
